item.title: Texans star celebrates Abbott's defeat with an NSFW message
item.description: Dalton Schultz, who has been with the Houston Texans since 2023 has let his feelings towards Greg Abbott known. (Tim Warner/Getty Images) This Texans star has a blunt message for Greg Abbott after the longtime Texas governor's election defeat. Texas was swept up in a blue wave on Tuesday night, with Democrats breaking the hold Republicans had on Texas politics for the past 30 years. Texans tight end Dalton Schultz celebrated the news by giving the outgoing Texas governor a two-word send-off on his Instagram story. "Get F---ed!," Schultz wrote on his Instagram story on Wednesday morning, tagging Abbott in the post. The Texans player followed up his insult to Abbott by showing his support for the newly elected Texas governor, Gina Hinojosa. Reactions to Schultz's position surprised fans who were unaware of Schultz political standing, with many fans saying his post warranted a jersey purchase "That's my tight end," one fan wrote on X. "Damn, no more Dalton Schultzslander lol," another fan wrote. "We have our Joe Rogan of the Left," another chimed in. AUSTIN, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 3: Gov. Greg Abbott hugs his wife, Cecilia, and their daughter, Audrey, after delivering a concession speech during an election night event at Speakeasy in Austin on Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. (Jay Janner/The Austin American-Statesman via Getty Images) (Austin American-Statesman/Hearst/Austin American-Statesman via Ge) Schultz, who has been with the Texans since 2023 after spending four seasons with the Dallas Cowboys, holds the franchise record for most receptions by a tight end. He has also made his opinions about Greg Abbott and his policies abundantly clear for some time now. In a tweet from February 23, 2022, Schultz criticized Abbott for issuing a directive ordering the Texas Department of Family and Protective Services to treat and classify medically necessary gender affirming care for transgender youth as child abuse "If you think anything about what the POS [Greg Abbott] is doing about Trans kids in Texas is ok or justified, please unfollow me," Schultz wrote on X. If you think anything about what the POS @GregAbbott_TX is doing about Trans kids in Texas is ok or justified, please unfollow me. - Dalton Schultz (@BinghamBaller9) February 23, 2022 In July 2022, Schultz called out the Texas governor once again, quoting a tweet from the official Texas governor account blaming the deaths of migrants on President Joe Biden. Never heard of a good leader who points fingers, Greg. - Dalton Schultz (@BinghamBaller9) June 28, 2022 Schultz, who graduated from Stanford University in 2017, also criticized the two-party system that exists in the United States in May of 2022, calling it "broken" and "beyond frustrating as a US citizen." His political posting on X has slowed since 2022, but the Texas Democrats' massive victory and Greg Abbott's defeat apparently warranted a social media victory lap. item.title: Kyle Farmer’s 2026 Season: A Short Stint With Big Wasted Potential
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Kyle Farmer spent most of 2026 on the Atlanta Braves roster, yet he barely touched the field. The veteran infielder arrived in early February hoping to help his hometown club, but his time in the big leagues was short and quiet. He played only 14 games all season, a number that shocked fans who expected him to be a key backup. His path from signing to release tells a story of missed chances and a roster that simply did not need him. The Braves brought him in as a free agent in early February 2026, only to cut him and re-sign him a month later in March. Per Battery Power , he was meant to be an end-of-bench option who could fill in at shortstop or catch in an emergency. Instead, he sat on the bench for weeks, saw limited action, and landed on the injured list by mid-May. When he returned on July 4, he got just one plate appearance before the team released him on July 21. He signed a minor league deal later and came back in September, but his season was already over. A Roster Spot That Went Unused Farmer made the Opening Day roster, but that spot meant little when he could not get into games. He played ten games over six weeks and got only 15 plate appearances. His return in July lasted two games with one at-bat before he was let go. Even his late-season call-up in September brought just two games and three more plate appearances. In total, he slashed .222/.211/.278 with a 25 wRC+, numbers that show he could not hit at all. He finished with -0.1 fWAR, marking his second straight season below replacement level. On April 30, acting as the designated hitter at home versus the Detroit Tigers, he made his single start. He went 1-for-3 in that game, which was his best moment of the year. That single in the second inning helped score the first run, giving him a win probability added of 0.03. Per Battery Power, it has been two years since Farmer actually provided any value to a team. It was a tiny spark in a very dark season for a player who has played 97 or more games every year since 2019, except for 2020. Why The Experiment Failed The Braves hoped Farmer would be a safety net if Ha-Seong Kim got hurt, but the plan fell apart. He spent 2025 with the Colorado Rockies and had a terrible year with a -1.0 fWAR in 300 plate appearances. That bad season hurt his reputation before he even put on a Braves uniform. The team needed someone who could hit or play great defense, and Farmer did neither in his tiny sample. He played third base, second base, and shortstop but did nothing to stand out in any of those spots. At 36 years old, Farmer is past his prime, and the stats prove it. His career has been built on playing a lot of games, but he could not do that in 2026. The team gave him a chance to return to Atlanta, but they did not give him a real role to fill. item.title: Caitlin Clark reacts to encouraging Jack Campbell news
item.description: Oct 1, 2026; Las Vegas, Nevada, USA; Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark (22) walks on the court during the fourth quarter of game three of the first round for the 2026 WNBA Playoffs against the Las Vegas Aces at Michelob Ultra Arena. Mandatory Credit: Lucas Peltier-Imagn Images Many football fans have been keeping an eye on the story of Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell, who suffered a frightening neck injury during Sunday’s game. Caitlin Clark has added incentive to monitor Campbell’s progress. Not only are she and the 2025 All-Pro both Iowa Hawkeyes, but Campbell’s wife Megan played with Clark at Iowa during the 2020-21 season. On Wednesday afternoon, after Campbell announced he had full movement in his lower extremities and was “continuing to make progress” with moving his upper body, Clark sent a quick message of support to her former teammate. On her Instagram story , Clark shared ESPN and Adam Schefter’s post featuring Jack Campbell’s statement. Underneath it, she commented three blue hearts and tagged Megan. Once a Hawkeye Megan Campbell (née Meyer) was a star high school player in Mason City, Iowa before joining the Iowa program in 2019. In 2020-21, she was a key contributor off the bench while Clark became the team’s freshman sensation, scoring 26.6 points per game and leading the Hawkeyes to the Sweet 16. While Meyer transferred to Drake following the season and enjoyed a stellar 2021-22 campaign, she and Clark obviously still have a connection, judging by the latter’s social media post. ‘Optimistic’ Campbell working toward recovery Jack Campbell went down while making a tackle in the fourth quarter of the Lions’ win over the Minnesota Vikings. The 26-year-old linebacker lay motionless on the field for several minutes before being immobilized and taken off on a stretcher. The Lions had been vague on specifics regarding Campbell’s condition, only saying Monday that things were trending positively. Campbell himself provided the details in a statement earlier today. “I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better,” he said. “My faith in God has never been stronger. I know He has a plan for me, and I trust in that plan. I know there may be challenges ahead, but with my faith, my family, and so many people in my corner, I know we’ll get through this.” The post Caitlin Clark reacts to encouraging Jack Campbell news appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: Purple wave, blue wave: Valkyries parade doubles as election celebration
item.description: Valkyries' mascot Violet waves to fans in attendance to see the 2026 WNBA Champions at Jack London Square in Oakland, Calif. on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. Following the ceremony, the team will bring the WNBA Championship Trophy across the Bay to San Francisco for the parade. (Yalonda M. James/S.F. Chronicle) Giddy energy from Tuesday night's Democratic electoral sweep seemed only to grow Wednesday morning as revelers gathered for the Valkyries WNBA championship parade. That much was clear from the sign that Serena Poon held aloft as she stood on the ferry lawn at Jack London Square, where the players and their entourage would soon depart by boat to San Francisco. "Purple wave 10/31; Blue wave 11/2," it said, linking the team's come-from-behind victory on Halloween night to a national blowout by Democrats, one so overwhelming that pundits ran out of tidal metaphors to describe it. The connection seemed fitting when a procession of Democratic politicians strode down the Embarcadero to welcome the Valkyries players when their boat was set to dock near the Ferry Building at noon. Among the delegation: Sen. Adam Schiff, former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, state Sen. Scott Wiener (who is now leading in the race to succeed Pelosi) and Mayor Daniel Lurie in a violet shirt. For Poon, the political contact high was palpable. "We're just riding the high of Valks win, and then last night was just historic with blue wave," she said. "It was like a blue tsunami, and I'm just so stoked." Every Embarcadero-bound BART train and Muni bus became a purple and black menagerie as fans flocked in with jerseys, feathery boas and birdlike headdresses. If the attire seemed apolitical, the placards were not. Beth Jaeger of San Francisco arrived at the Embarcadero at 8 a.m. dressed as a Valkyrie, complete with purple face paint - and a sign that said "In a world of Sophies, be a Gabby." The slogan referenced public comments by Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham, who has insisted that trans women should be barred from the WNBA. Henry, from Oakland, holds a sign celebrating both the Valkyries' championship and Democrats' sweeping wins in Tuesday's midterm election. (Saul Pink / S.F. Chronicle) On the back of Jaeger's sign: "Welcome to the Gay Area." Others echoed pro-LGBTQ messages that, while not directly tied to an election wedge issue on Tuesday, generally defied the Trump Administration's stances on gender politics and diversity. As the morning wore on, "Gay Area" logos proliferated along the Embarcadero: in shimmery ink on card stock, emblazoned on T-shirts, embroidered on denim jackets, scrawled onto decals. "It was already so hopeful to see them win, and then to see and then to see so much hope across the country," said Cat De La Pena of San Jose, dangling her own hand-made "Gay Area" sign with a portrait of Valkyries forward and championship MVP Gabby Williams, arms outstretched to sink a 3-pointer into the basket. A 17th player is permitted as long as he qualifies for the NFL’s International Pathway Program. Players with no accrued seasons (rookies) and those with fewer than nine regular-season games in their lone accrued season. A maximum of ten players are allowed who have earned no more than two accrued seasons. Up to six players with unlimited accrued seasons are permitted on the practice squad. However, the number of players in the last two categories cannot exceed 10 total players. Teams can elevate up to two practice squad players for each game, but they can still only have 48 players active on game day. After the game, the elevated player(s) will revert to the practice squad. A player can be elevated up to three times, but if he’s needed after that, the team would be required to sign him to the 53-man active roster. Players on practice squads are free agents who can be signed to another team’s active roster. A player’s current club can’t block him from leaving; they can only make a counteroffer to keep him. Ultimately, it’s the player’s decision. If a player is signed away, his new team must keep him on its 53-man roster for three weeks, but if he’s released, he’ll revert to his previous team. Players signed to another active roster are also guaranteed three weeks’ salary. A practice squad player can’t sign with his team’s upcoming opponent unless he does so six days before the upcoming game or ten days prior if his team is on its bye week.

item.title: Dianna Russini reportedly returning to sports media ‘next week’
item.description: Credit: The Dan Patrick Show Dianna Russini has apparently kept herself on the sidelines long enough. The former top NFL insider for The Athletic who became embroiled in scandal this offseason after numerous photos surfaced showing her cozy and seemingly intimate relationship with New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel is set to return “next week” according to a report by Mike Florio in Pro Football Talk . “Per a source with knowledge of the situation, Russini has begun getting the word out to people in the league that she’ll be returning to work ‘next week,'” Florio reports, indicating that it is “unclear” for what outlet she’ll be working for, or what job she will be doing. Russini resigned from The Athletic in April, one week after the New York Post published the first batch of photos showing her and Vrabel together at a high-end resort in Arizona. In her letter of resignation, Russini maintained that there was no foul play between her and Vrabel. “Rather than allowing this [scandal] to continue, I have decided to step aside now – before my current contract expires on June 30. I do so not because I accept the narrative that has been constructed around this episode, but because I refuse to lend it further oxygen or to let it define me or my career,” Russini wrote at the time. Last month, the New York Post reported that Russini had hired crisis management expert Melissa Nathan , one of the first signs that the veteran NFL reporter was eyeing a return to media. Russini has not made any public statements since her resignation in April. Whether Russini will return in a capacity that relies on her credibility as a reporter, or in a role that is more personality-focused, is unclear. No doubt, Russini maintains a large rolodex of contacts throughout the league, though those sources’ willingness to speak candidly with her might be compromised after the scandal. Russini has long been able to hold court in more casual settings, however, and would likely command an audience even without dishing out NFL scoops. item.title: Valkyries star Gabby Williams reveals Michael Jordan reached out to her after WNBA championship win
item.description: Valkyries star Gabby Williams reveals Michael Jordan reached out to her after WNBA championship win originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Michael Jordan knows a thing or two about winning, and Gabby Williams was in for a surprise of a lifetime when he reached out to congratulate her. The Golden State Valkyries star defeated the Atlanta Dream in Game 7 of the WNBA Finals, the first time that the league was pushed to the last qualifier round in the series. Williams, a forward for the Valkyries, shared that Jordan reached out to her to congratulate her on her first-ever WNBA championship win. “My Jordan rep agent texted me, and he was just like, ‘Just so you know, it’s not spam, but you’re gonna get a text,’ ” Williams told People about the moment. “And I was driving, and I was like, ‘Do not crash your car, do not crash your car. Get to the gym, get to the parking lot.’” Williams added that the six-time NBA champion praised her for becoming a WNBA champion. “He congratulated me, and said it’d been an amazing season and just told me, ‘Stay hungry.’ ” she told the outlet. “That felt like a very Michael Jordan thing to say.” Williams also left with the WNBA Finals MVP title after the thrilling 68–63 Game 7 victory over the Dream. She also praised their head coach, Natalie Nakase, for leading the team to the franchise's first-ever win. "Coach Nat is the most competitive person I've ever met in my entire life. But she is competitive in everything that she does, you know, even how she treats people, even how she shows up every day, and we all feed off of that," Williams said. "I think she's a leader by example. She cares so, so deeply on a human level for each person, and you just want to go through a wall for her." item.title: Meet the Shasta Family YMCA Athletes of the Week winners for Oct. 25-31
item.description: Two Shasta County athletes are being recognized for their outstanding achievements on the field and court. This week, Foothill and Redding Christian high school athletes are being highlighted. It's time to meet the two Shasta Family YMCA Athletes of the Week for their accomplishments over the week of Oct. 25-31. Turner Knowles, Foothill Sport : Football School : Foothill Class : Senior Team Contributions : Foothill running back Turner Knowles had a career day in a wild Week 9 win over Enterprise. Knowles rushed for 273 yards and 5 touchdowns — both set new career highs — to lead the Cougars to a 51-42 win over the Hornets. Knowles extended his season total to 1,277 yards and 21 touchdowns, good for the sixth most rushing yards and third most touchdowns scored by a skill position player. Knowles is one of the best running backs in the section, and he put it on display in the Cougars win over the Hornets. It was the second time Knowles rushed for over 200 yards this season and the third time he's scored at least 4 touchdowns in a game. Aliyah Mendoza, Redding Christian Sport : Volleyball School : Redding Christian Class : Senior Team Contributions : In the Lions Northern Section quarterfinal matchup against Fall River, senior outside hitter Aliyah Mendoza racked up 20 kills in four sets (5 kills per set) to help send her team to the semifinals. Mendoza also added 3 digs and 6 serve receptions in Redding Christian's 3-1 win over the Bulldogs. In a Nov. 3 win over Maxwell, Mendoza recorded 8 kills, 1 ace, 4 digs, 1 assist and 17 serve receptions as the Lions advanced to the Northern Section championship game. Mendoza's 257 kills this season rank 28th in the section and second in Division VI. Her 20 kills against Maxwell were the second most kills Mendoza has recorded in her varsity career. She helped lead the Lions to a 27-3 record and will compete for the NSCIF Division VI title on Saturday, Nov. 7. item.title: Brewers Should Avoid Signing Jake Bauers To Multi-Year Deal
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers first baseman Jake Bauers Jake Bauers had a breakout season at 30 years old, and the Milwaukee Brewers extended him the qualifying offer. If Bauers accepts his one-year, $23.15 million offer, the Brewers don't have any choice to make. He will be back at that price. However, after the year he had, he should have a couple of multi-year offers on the table as well. The Brewers do not need to be one of the teams making one of those offers. Having Bauers back for one season would be great, because if he is unable to replicate his career year, they would be clear of him. There is a chance that his 2026 season ends up being something like Trent Grisham's 2025 season. Every team will need to decide whether they believe Bauers has finally figured out the big leagues with his new approach to the game or if last season was a fluke. The rest of the league may let the Brewers be the team that has to figure it out by making Bauers accept the qualifying offer. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! As far as keeping Bauers past next season, the Brewers have no need to. Not only do they have Andrew Fischer, Blake Burke and Luke Adams capable of playing first base knocking on the door of the big leagues, but they also have Andrew Vaughn who could be a potential option past next season. Bauers will be expensive to keep on a multi-year deal, and could really block some prospects the team views fondly. The Brewers should not change the way they do business just because they won the World Series. Bauers was a great player for them, and his efforts won't be forgotten. Ultimately, bringing him back for one more year won't hurt their long-term plans, and it will minimize the damage if his breakout proves to be a fluke. item.title: Dianna Russini finally returning to sports media after Mike Vrabel scandal
item.description: Next week will mark the halfway point in the NFL season, and apparently, also the return of Dianna Russini to sports media after she stepped down from her role with The Athletic in the wake of the scandal involving her and New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel that dominated the offseason. “Russini’s relationship with Vrabel was in clear violation of The Athletic ’s standards,” The Athletic’s Mike Semel, who conducted an internal investigation, said of the controversy. “Regardless of whether the relationship was romantic, it was a breach and should have been disclosed.” According to Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio, a “source with knowledge of the situation” has made it known that Russini has made it clear to people around the league that she’ll make her return “next week” The news comes after Russini reportedly hired infamous publicist Melissa Nathan, a veteran of multiple infamous Hollywood imbroglios, but one who isn’t without her own controversy, as she is facing perjury allegations due to her involvement in the incredibly messy situation between Blake Lively and Justin Baldoni. Many prominent figures across sports media also anticipated that Russini’s return to sports media was imminent. In August, Mike Silver sang her praises and predicted her return. “Really good friend of mine,” he said of Russini. “Worked with her at The Athletic for too short of a time, unfortunately. Really, really proud of the journalism we did together and honestly just really bummed that we don’t get to continue it because we worked really well together. “I don’t think people understand the level of elite that she was performing at in terms of keeping in touch with the really important people around the league. And I don’t mean just agents and transactional, like players, coaches, owners, all of it, talking, having real conversations with them every day and really knowing what was going on and competing at a very high level. “I do miss having her a lot. Very bummed that it all imploded. She became a very high-profile person. I’m not a super judgy person. I would never comment on tabloid crap.” Silver then praised her family, and predicted that when she returned, it’d be in a role other than an NFL insider. “And I do think she’s going to be back, probably not as an insider, at least in the short term. But I think she’ll be back in this realm, probably talking about football and other things pretty soon,” he said. It would seem we’ll know immenently just what capacity she’ll be back in. item.title: Could Queen City Quarter become an everyday destination in Uptown Charlotte?
item.description: The Charlotte Hornets are part of an ownership group that purchased the former EpiCentre complex in Uptown Charlotte, now known as Queen City Quarter, for $27.5 million. The purchase price covers a property with an estimated value of nearly $100 million. Sports analysts consider the three-company venture well financed. Erik Spanberg, a reporter with the Sports Business Journal, noted that the acquisition follows earlier municipal approvals for facility upgrades. “I don’t think many of us knew that the Charlotte Hornets were going to be part of the buying group,” Spanberg said. He added that “it started when the city approved the arena renovations and the training center,” explaining that “teams want to surround their arenas and stadiums with things that they develop and own.” PREVIOUS COVERAGE: Former EpiCentre site Queen City Quarter undergoes major change Rick Schnall, co-owner of the Charlotte Hornets, hinted in May that broader developments were being considered alongside basketball facilities. “From the beginning, this project is more than it is not just about basketball,” Schnall said. “It’s about continuing momentum in Uptown Charlotte in the city of Charlotte and strengthening the Spectrum Center and the community around it.” Other NBA franchises have pursued similar arena-adjacent real estate projects. In 2015, the Sacramento Kings entered a joint venture to redevelop a plaza into 1 million square feet of space known as Downtown Commons, or DOCO, surrounding the Golden one Center. According to the developer, that project influenced $6.7 billion in new projects by 2022, while bringing 150 retail businesses, residential units, hotels, restaurants, and increased foot traffic to the area. Spanberg noted that multiple franchises have executed comparable development projects around their venues. “In the NBA, you’ve seen not only Sacramento, but you’ve also seen Milwaukee Bucks do it really well with the beer district. You’ve seen the Indiana Pacers do it recently,” Spanberg said. He added that the long-term challenge for such projects lies in sustained activity. “The question always is, can you do it to an extent where people want to come not just on game day, but every day,” Spanberg said. Similar developments are also underway elsewhere in North Carolina. A new entertainment district is planned in Raleigh surrounding the Lenovo Center. According to the Sports Business Journal , those plans feature thousands of housing units, dining areas, and an enhanced tailgating experience for Carolina Hurricanes fans.

That’s going to have their fanbase circling every big name that might be available in an effort to improve the roster, and that includes Detroit Red Wings center Dylan Larkin. Larkin requested a trade after last season ended, but he still hasn’t been moved. The Sabres aren’t on Larkin’s 10-team approved trade list, yet that hasn’t stopped speculation that he could still end up in Buffalo. And I do think it’s fair to expect Kekäläinen to make a significant deal at some point this season. item.title: 'The objective is clear' - Aston Villa send firm message to Manchester United as Unai Emery commits beyond 2029
item.description: Unai Emery Aston Villa - Getty Aston Villa have publicly confirmed that Unai Emery is committed to the club beyond 2029 after positive talks with chairman Nassef Sawiris, ending speculation over a move to Manchester United. The Spaniard has been strongly linked with replacing Michael Carrick at Old Trafford, where Villa travel this weekend in need of a response to Tuesday's 3-0 Champions League defeat to Barcelona. Aston Villa confirm Emery commitment amid Manchester United links Villa have moved to end speculation over Emery's future, releasing a statement on Wednesday that confirmed a clear commitment beyond 2029 following talks between the manager and club chiefs. The 55-year-old has been strongly linked with replacing Carrick at Manchester United . According to The Telegraph, Emery is in advanced talks over a new deal at Villa, which would nip rumours of a move to Old Trafford in the bud. It would have cost United £20 million to release him from his current contract. Villa statement reveals details of key meeting Emery's impressive four-year spell at Villa prompted talks with Sawiris, president of football operations Roberto Olabe and director of football operations Damian Vidagany over his long-term future. In a very transparent statement, the club confirmed the meeting had produced "positive discussions", with their update reading: "Aston Villa held an important working meeting today to plan the club's future and lay the foundations for its long-term sporting and institutional project. "The meeting brought together Nassef Sawiris, the club's Chairman and Unai Emery alongside President of Football Operations Roberto Olabe and Director of Football Operations Damian Vidagany. Emery set to stay at Villa into the next decade "The discussions focused on jointly planning the club's long-term strategic direction, with positive discussions establishing a clear commitment beyond 2029 for the joint development of the club under the sporting leadership of Unai Emery based on the shared ambitions and common goal to reach excellency and keep growing during the next years. "The objective is clear: to build an ambitious, competitive Aston Villa capable of taking on the biggest challenges and achievements." Emery signed a five-year contract extension in May 2024, 18 months after joining, but he now looks set to remain in charge heading into the next decade. What next for Emery, Villa and Carrick? Emery will be at Old Trafford this weekend when United host Villa, whose 3-0 loss to Barcelona and draw with Fulham last Saturday leave them needing a positive result before the November international break. United had won just two games all season before Tuesday's sensational 3-2 comeback triumph over AS Roma, and another victory could keep Carrick in the role beyond the break, when his performances are due to be reviewed.

item.title: Hornets Reveal Kon Knueppel’s Final Status Ahead of Nets Matchup
item.description: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - SEPTEMBER 28: Kon Knueppel #7 poses for a photo opportunity during the Charlotte Hornets Media Day at Novant Health Performance Center on September 28, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) Getty The Charlotte Hornets (3-5) are struggling to gain footing at the beginning of the 2026-27 season. Charlotte currently holds the worst offense in the NBA eight games in. There’s reasoning behind this current mark, including in early injuries to core players. Two of the five starting players for the Hornets (Coby White, Kon Knueppel) have been out thus far due to different injuries. In a sign of progress, Charlotte is making a final call on the latter as of Wednesday afternoon. Hornets Make Final Call on Star Wing The Hornets official PR account ( via X ) is ruling that Knueppel will make his season debut on Wednesday against the Brooklyn Nets . Knueppel, 21, has been working his way back from a left hamstring strain. The season debut is setting up to be a major breath of fresh air for a Charlotte offense that needs life. Knueppel’s season debut should carry much weight. His 273 three-point connections as a rookie led the NBA. This, along with progression that should come with more experience alongside teammates such as Brandon Miller , should breed more positive results. What Knueppel’s Return Means For Rest of Rotation The obvious fallout from Knueppel coming back is that he will obviously be in the starting lineup. However, there are deeper implications than just starting. Players that were seeing a decent volume of playing time have a chance to sink in the rotation. The player that might face the most negative impact is Grayson Allen . Allen, a Duke alum the same as Knueppel, has been the early-season alternative – particularly as a three-point marksmen. The immediate need for Allen to eat minutes subsides now, although he still provides value as a playmaker. It will be fascinating to see how head coach Charles Lee operates in this situation. item.title: Everything Luke Fickell said after Badgers loss to Iowa
item.description: Wisconsin head coach Luke Fickell leads his team to the field before their game against Notre Dame Sunday, September 6, 2026 at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Wisconsin Badgers were embarrassed 30-0 by the Iowa Hawkeyes in yet another rivalry game flop, as they fell to 5-3 on the season and 3-2 in conference play. It was a game where Wisconsin lost on every side and was awfully reminiscent of the team’s previous two losses to Iowa. Luke Fickell has now been outscored 124-16 in his four games at Wisconsin against Iowa. After the game, Fickell spoke with the media, outlining his frustrations and sharing his thoughts on the game. Here’s everything he said after the loss on Saturday. Opening Statement Well, that’s an old-fashioned ass whooping, and it doesn’t feel good. Were we prepared? Were we not prepared? We didn’t play like we were prepared today. They asked me if there were any positives, and I said I don’t know that I could find any positives in the way that we played, the way we performed. Yeah, they kept battling no matter what, but that’s a foregone conclusion. You have to do that. It’s, do you battle with the intent? Do you have the intensity to understand what it’s going to be like when you walk into this place and what you have to do in order to not just win, but make this a game? And we did none of that today. It’s very, very disappointing. I’m not sitting here saying I’ve got any answers for you. I’m not pointing any fingers at anybody because all three phases of the game, we were completely manhandled for 60-plus minutes. On why this keeps happening vs. Iowa… I don’t know. We made an overemphasis on it in the past, on the rivalry and what we needed to be able to do all of spring football and all of winter and all of fall. And then this year, it’s like, look, let’s make sure we understand, we respect the rivalry, but we don’t overdo something that is going to put us in a position where we play too emotional and can’t play 60-plus minutes. And we didn’t do that either. I think first of all, you’ve got to win the line of scrimmage. And I know that we can honestly say for the last couple years, we have not done that. And so anything beyond that, there’s a lot of other things, but that’s where it starts and that’s where it has been. And we didn’t do that either. I think first of all, you’ve got to win the line of scrimmage. And I know that we can honestly say for the last couple years, we have not done that. And so anything beyond that, there’s a lot of other things, but that’s where it starts and that’s where it has been. On whether Iowa’s recent dominance has affected Wisconsin’s confidence in the rivalry… No, I don’t. There’s so many guys here that don’t even know or understand what’s happened the last couple years. We explained it and talked about it and went through some of those things, but they didn’t live it. So it’s not like they have some shell shock of some remembrance of what has happened. I don’t think that’s the case. It’s just the sheer fact that we didn’t play today. Whether there’s an arrogance and a delusion coming off of last week that we felt like we were in a different place, I hope we have more maturity than that. But surely it didn’t look like it today. On the decision to replace Colton Joseph at quarterback… I just thought it was an opportunity, and it was some time we needed to try to find a way to have a little bit of a spark. The situation was where it was. We weren’t able to run the football, so we felt like, hey, look, I don’t know that we need to keep Colton in there and keep trying to run him to see if he can get us going. Let’s give the young kid an opportunity. Let’s see if we can find any spark and some things that we need to see. But they’re real because if you put them on film, you’ve got to own them. item.title: Billions in revenue proves Fifa right on the World Cup – but only on things it cares about
item.description: The 2026 edition of the tournament brought in untold amounts of money to Gianni Infantino’s governing body The total hasn’t entirely stopped rising yet, still clicking away towards a final tally. Still, Fifa has already announced that it surpassed its own lofty revenue projections for the 2026 World Cup, bringing in $15bn, significantly more than anticipated. It appears that a third of that total – $5bn – came from ticket sales and hospitality alone, per reporting from the Times . That would mean direct income from the matchgoing fans came in five times as high in the United States, Canada and Mexico as it did at the last World Cup, in Qatar in 2022, when the total stood at $929m. While 2026’s expanded World Cup added 40 games to the schedule, the takings nevertheless went from an average of about $14.5m per match to about $48m. Continue reading...

item.title: Mainoo and Lacey raise the spirits but systemic change still required at Manchester United | Nick Ames
item.description: There were protests at Old Trafford and even though two academy products stood out, Michael Carrick’s future is far from safe Green and yellow balloons bobbed around the Stretford End. Tennis balls rained down on the pitch in protest at the chronic, enduringly cinematic decline presided over by Manchester United’s ownership. Then came a reminder of the humble football’s extraordinary power to bend history, minds and wills. United’s players departed victorious having somehow won the game within the game, separating themselves from the fog of unhappy context swirling on all sides and turning the second half into its own soaring, ripping story for the ages. Will it be enough to save Michael Carrick, who was once again serenaded when minds wandered from the joint scourges of the Glazer family and Jim Ratcliffe? If Aston Villa defend a shade more competently than Roma on Sunday then perhaps not. United have led their supporters, remarkable in their tenor of backing for players and head coach here, up more than enough false peaks over the past 13 years. Arguably, that is one reason for Carrick being given the job on a permanent basis. Continue reading...

item.title: Lennart Karl steals in behind Atlético Madrid to inspire Bayern Munich win
item.description: “This stadium brings back bad memories but I hope to be able to replace them with good ones,” Harry Kane had said on Monday night, and 24 hours later this was a start. A small step, perhaps, towards coming back on 5 June and having a second go at winning the Champions League in the arena where he lost the 2019 final . On his first European outing since winning the Ballon d’Or , the England captain was unable to score but he and his Bayern Munich team defeated Atlético Madrid, fellow semi-finalists from last season. They did so in a way that suggests that their candidacy this season is serious. It may not have been sparkling but they had been superior almost from the start, dominant in physique and football. This is a team with few weaknesses, intense and impressive throughout. All Atlético could do was resist and it never truly felt like they would be able to do that for ninety minutes; ultimately, they lasted 54. That was when Lennart Karl scored the first. The superb Konrad Laimer then added the second on a night when they racked up nineteen shots. It had been heavy going for a while, and they had been made to wait, but in the end Bayern were just that bit too good. Continue reading...

While Football Daily hasn’t actually seen much of West Ham this season, we’ve noted enough of their results to presume they were doing OK in their attempt to bounce back to the Premier League after relegation. Less than a third of the way through the Championship season under Nuno Espírito Santo, they’d already spanked six without reply past both Wrexham and Lincoln, while scoring three or more in wins over Wolves, Derby and Bolton. However, it turns out that of the 13 matches they’ve played in a league that is famously difficult to get out of (unless you were Sheffield Wednesday last season ), they have actually lost three times and currently sit in eighth place, a whopping six points off leaders Middlesbrough. Given the context of such an unbridgeable chasm, it is small wonder West Ham fans woke up to news that Nuno had been unceremoniously bounced out of the London Stadium with a P45 in hand. While my heart aches for Jesús de Miguel, who has died after a collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono, I shudder to think the trauma that shall haunt Owono for the rest of his life. I do hope and pray the wider community understands and extends their support in his recuperation” – Krishna Moorthy. As an upgrade to Steve Plever’s suggestion of paper thin shirts [ Monday’s letters ]: how about Velcro shirts? If the bit comes off, it is a shirt pull and the offender has the honour of putting it back in place before being awarded a yellow card” – Mike Harold. To dive or not to dive seems to be biggest dilemma in the Premier League right now. It’s not. The problem with today’s highly paid professionals is that they simply have no panache at all when they go down. I recall watching Francis Lee pick up the ball on the halfway line at a mud soaked Maine Road in the late 1960s, he put his head down and headed for goal, he was determined, he was single minded. He was 30 yards from goal, he was in full flow. He was tackled from behind and then he really took off, he grew wings, he soared. I swear he landed in the penalty area over 10 yards away. He dragged himself to his feet and without a semblance of a smile smashed the well-deserved penalty, with a very heavy leather ball straight at the centre of the goal at over 70 mph. The goalkeeper, obviously no fool, simply dived out of the way. The press christened him “Lee Won Pen” He was my hero. That man had panache, he had style” – Myles Flynn. I am interested to read that Aston Villa considered the words of Jamie Carragher “unacceptable insults” . It would obviously help matters if they could publish examples of acceptable insults” – Rupert Jeffery. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. The season of domination that many anticipated from the champions appears to be coming to pass. Liverpool challenged them on Sunday. There was a 20-minute spell before half-time when they swarmed all over Arsenal, and Anfield felt at least like it did in the golden years of Jürgen Klopp, when it buzzed with an energy that could overwhelm visitors. item.title: Unai Simón caps myth-making week with another extraordinary night | Sid Lowe
item.description: Athletic’s win over Real Sociedad was culmination of six unique days for the Spain keeper after night at the Palladium For the third time in six days everyone got to their feet to hand a standing ovation to Unai Simón, dressed in all black, before the world. Named the best men’s goalkeeper on the planet, holding the Lev Yashin trophy, they had applauded him at the London Palladium on Monday night and before the game began at San Mamés, Bilbao, on Sunday. Now somewhere in the middle of it all, the ferocity of the 197th Basque derby, there was another moment, even more meaningful and more lasting, a cheer again giving way to something deeper: an appreciation for a man as well as his work closing a week that will be forever his. Which means it will be forever theirs too. Real Sociedad and Athletic Club had been doing battle for 72 minutes and it was 2-1 when Simon took off to make a save that denied Carlos Soler an equaliser and defied belief . As the ball flew off his palm, San Mamés exploded. And then it happened: never mind that Athletic still had a derby to win and a corner to defend, forget the fact that the lead was a single goal, the visitors relentless now and 25 minutes still to resist; at the stadium everyone calls the Cathedral , a place of ritual and liturgy like no other, the entire congregation, 50,092 people, started clapping. Started and did not stop. For a minute, maybe more, it was like the match that matters most didn’t matter at all, momentarily fading until it was just him and them together. Continue reading...

item.title: Roster rifts, police raids and Son’s uncertain future leave South Korea at a crossroads
item.description: After a disaster World Cup, the team have continued to spiral, with tensions high between young and older players and the captain’s standing in question Son Heung-min and Cristiano Ronaldo are iconic No 7s, Premier League legends and international record-breakers. Now there is a surprising danger of them having something else in common: being a divisive presence in their national teams. On 21 October, during a parliamentary committee meeting, politician Jeong Yeon-wook put a question to acting Korea Football Association (KFA) president Lee Yong-soo, that took a story out of the sports pages and into the national conversation. “It is said that recently, within the national team squad, players have been calling him not by his name but as ‘No 7’ or ‘that person’. Do you know who that is?” Lee then replied, “Are you referring to Son Heung-min?” Jeong went on: “So it appears to be true. … It has also been revealed that the national team’s leadership is causing discord and has broken down overall.” Lee declined to comment. item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.content:encoded: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
